result.title: Agents Cannot Hand Over What They Have Not Yet Understood
result.summary: Agents that work beyond a single context window, or in teams, hand their work to a successor as a short written summary. Evaluation has focused on whether an agent can solve a task, and relatively little is known about how much of what an agent has learned survives being written down. We study this in 56 interactive worlds with hidden rules, where an agent that is told nothing fails and an agent given a 300-character statement of the rules succeeds. We compare one agent that plays eight lives and keeps its whole history with a chain of eight agents that each play one life and inherit a 300-character note. All six models we test learn less in the chain: after eight generations it stands where the single agent stood after about four lives. Controlled variants of the chain decompose this handoff loss into three components: none from changing the agent, a smaller loss from compressing to 300 characters, and a larger loss from compressing repeatedly. When each note is written from the full record of earlier lives instead of from the previous note, the same 300 characters recover 70% to 82% of the loss. The loss is robust across model sizes and is not alleviated by instructing the writer to record evidence, to revise the inherited note, or to keep a structured ledger. In simpler terms, an agent cannot hand over what it has not yet understood: a note holds what its writer has worked out, and a rule that takes several lives to see is lost with the lives that were not passed on.

AI.brief_summary: 在56个含隐藏规则的交互世界中，比较单个 agent 连打八条命并保留完整历史，与八个 agent 各打一条命、每次继承300字符笔记；发现链式交接学到的东西明显更少，并把损失受控分解为更换 agent、单次压缩和反复压缩三部分，指出从完整历史重写笔记可挽回大部分损失。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“状态被压成短文本再多次传递”的受控拆解可供核查 latent 状态在多步更新与监督中的信息坍缩与贡献分配，但对象是纯文本 agent、无视觉与 latent 表征，迁移线索需人工评估。
